name: ClipMaster
description:
Clipboard history for GNOME Shell.

ClipMaster reads the clipboard so it can give you back what you copied an hour ago. That history stays on your computer: the extension has no network code, no telemetry and no account.

Press your shortcut, type a word to find the entry, press Enter to paste it. Or press 1 to 9 and skip the search.

* Text, links, colours, code and images, with thumbnails
* Search, favourites, pinned items and custom lists
* Private mode: one switch, and nothing is recorded until you turn it off again
* A per application exclusion list, so a password manager never reaches the history
* Any entry as a QR code, which is the quickest way to get a link onto a phone
* Twelve themes, or follow the system light and dark setting
* A resizable popup that opens at the pointer or at a fixed corner of the screen
* Optional obfuscation of the stored file. Obfuscation, not encryption: the key sits beside the data.

Supports GNOME Shell 46 to 51, on Wayland and X11.

New in 2.0: the popup opens again on GNOME 50 and 51, a history file that cannot be read is never overwritten, the excluded applications list actually works, and there is no keyboard shortcut set by default, because a clipboard extension is not allowed to claim one. Pick yours on the Shortcuts page.
